bull_bear.body:
- Heavily funding-constrained year; promoter putting in INR 85 cr via **optionally convertible instrument** (priced INR 110 vs SEBI floor INR 92 vs book value INR 109 — 20% premium; structured as OCI because promoters can only "creep" 5%/yr). Neo equity INR 30 cr (shareholder-approved).
- Priority: complete Jagriti, then refinance/exit the high-cost Neo debt in 15–16 months and lower cost of capital. No dividend focus mentioned — cash conservation / cost-cut mode ("magnifying lens" on costs).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **High-cost debt:** ~16.95% effective; if turnaround slips, interest eats earnings (investor concern raised twice). Exit depends on Jagriti + food-services recovery, not just refinancing.
- **Execution / commissioning slippage:** PM4 already delayed once on funding; "4 plants simultaneously" overstretched the team (admitted) — single most important catalyst is Sep commissioning + ramp.
- **Pricing war / waste-paper competition:** low-cost waste-paper producers (regulatory loophole) pressuring wrap-and-carry NSR; demand-supply mismatch as new supply enters.
- **Flexible-paper R&D risk:** repeatedly delayed ("taken longer than envisaged"); still at pilot — the highest-value optionality is unproven.
- **Food-services profitability:** still loss-making; relies on asset-light pivot + B2C/delivery working; "hockey-stick" promise unproven (15% market-share / ~INR 680 cr by 2028 goal reaffirmed but behind).
- **Credibility / governance:** management openly admitted "we are totally responsible for eroding your wealth," missed every commitment (1 bn USD by 2030, Guatemala, prior guidance); share price ~INR 300 vs ~INR 1,000 at peak investment.
- **Promoter pledge / guarantees:** shares pledged + personal/associate guarantees to Neo — leverage-on-promoter risk.
- **Working-capital tie-up post-PM4:** new WC limits needed; pledge sits with Neo (mitigant: WC lenders get first charge on current assets, no pledge).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Strikingly candid and apologetic — opened the call leading with "challenges and learnings," repeatedly took blame ("no one else to take the blame but us," "totally responsible for eroding your wealth"). Strategic re-focus is sensible (stabilize India, pause global, go asset-light, let converters coat). New hire Mayank Jindal (ex-JK Paper/APP, 35 yrs) adds operating credibility. But this is a "trust us / hockey-stick" story with a multi-year track record of missed commitments; promoter optimism is self-acknowledged ("how optimistic do you want me to be?"). Detailed, transparent funding explanation from Himanshu Kapoor. Tone = humble, rebuilding-credibility, execution-on-trial.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The funding fiasco was the root cause of nearly everything: faltering share price → Carnelian warrant failure → ~INR 300 cr hole → emergency high-cost Neo refinance → project delay → product-dev lag. The equity is now effectively a binary bet on Jagriti commissioning + cost of debt coming down in ~16 months.
- The real margin lever is **integrated-mill, low-cost base paper feeding higher-value grades** (release/glassine ~INR 130–150, then flexible ~INR 250–300/kg). Management explicitly says EBITDA % matters more than topline — hence the asset-light outsourcing push.
- Strategic humility: explicitly **letting converters do barrier coating** (vs in-house) to avoid channel conflict — a sober reversal of earlier ambition to own the full flexible stack.
- US (Pakka Inc.) and Guatemala greenfield are now optionality kept "alive but paused," not active capex — de-risks the near term but defers the "$1bn by 2030" dream.
- Watch the PM3 +10 tpd / +INR 8 cr PBT (June) as the first cheap, near-certain earnings recovery before Jagriti.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body:
- **Wrap & Carry / specialty paper (PM1/PM2/PM3):** PM3 = largest machine, ~50% of volume; 40-day outage was the year's main wound. Pricing war from new entrants + low-cost **waste-paper-based** producers (regulatory loophole: sold as "secondary" packaging but touches food) eroding the traditional wrap-and-carry market. Mitigation: product-mix shift to higher-contribution grades, cost optimization, specialized niches (some grown 50→400–500 t/month).
- **Food Services / Moulded ("Chuk"):** revenue growth real (vol +20%, B2C +2.5x, +25 cities) but loss-making on plant equipment issues + clean-up write-offs. Pivot to **asset-light outsourcing** (supply own bulk, contract-manufacture locally — cuts cost, freight, no capex, faster). Ayodhya moulded plant to be **refurbished/paused** (equipment removed/sold/leased; food-services production may pause at company's own end). New categories (delivery containers — soft-launched at "Akhtar", phase-1 launch this quarter; broader food-services range).
- **Project Jagriti (PM4):** brand-new paper machine for specialty "full-gate"/release-glassine base paper (~100 tpd base paper added) + new recovery boiler + power boiler + 15 MW turbine; pulping capacity up 130→180 t. Peak capacity 350–500 tpd. Integrated-mill cost advantage is the thesis.

business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- Historical EBITDA ~22–25% / ~INR 80–85 cr (FY23–25); FY26 collapsed on shutdown + pricing + write-offs. Recovery path: PM3 +INR 8 cr PBT, integrated-mill scale, higher-contribution product mix, return to 22–25% EBITDA.
- SG&A + team cost currently ~29–32% of sales (~INR 115–120 cr); expected to rise only to ~INR 160–180 cr (not 200) as the new plant scales, dropping the ratio to ~26–27% on +INR 200 cr topline.
- Working capital: incremental need from Jagriti modest (~INR 20–30 cr; pulping +50 t bagasse; finished stock 15–20 days paper / 25–30 days moulded) — total WC ~INR 45–50 cr, supported by internal accruals + existing current-account debtors.
- Funding cost is the near-term margin drag: 12% cash / 16.95% effective; management frames bank-debt alternative would also have cost ~INR 50–60 cr interest, so "delta not that much."
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** Turnaround/apology call. FY revenue dipped YoY (Q4 +8% YoY); wrap-and-carry vol -17% (PM3 40-day outage, -INR 11 cr PBT; pricing -INR 16 cr); food-services rev +~48% Q4 but loss-making + write-offs. Funding crisis fixed via Neo INR 500 cr NCD (+40 green-shoe) at 16.95% effective + promoter INR 85 cr OCI @ INR 110. Project Jagriti: boilers July, PM4 by end-Sep 2026. Guatemala + US near-shoring paused; focus = stabilize India, go asset-light. Target return to 22–25% EBITDA / INR 125–150 cr.
- _Next Q → check: (1) PM3 +10 tpd / +INR 8 cr PBT realized (June W4)? (2) power+recovery boiler commissioned July? (3) PM4 producing by end-Sep + ramp to 60%? (4) food-services back to profit on outsourcing pivot? (5) flexible/release-paper pilot results + first converter offtake; (6) any move to refinance/lower the Neo cost; (7) Oct in-person Ayodhya plant visit happened; (8) NSR recovery vs waste-paper competition._

outlook.body:
- **Project Jagriti commissioning:** power plant + recovery boiler commissioned ~July 2026; PM4 paper machine producing by **end-September 2026** (despite funding delays). PM3 capacity-increase pending work done in **4th week of June** (+10 t/day, ~+INR 8 cr PBT).
- **PM4 ramp:** ~60%+ capacity utilization by end-FY27 (this FY), ~75%+ next FY.
- **Revenue:** declined to give a hard number. Base ops ~INR 420 cr + 4–5 months of new-facility output + food-services growth (from ~INR 60 cr base). At full capacity Jagriti site: base paper ~INR 500 cr+; with molded upside ~INR 700–900 cr; **if flexibles crack: INR 1,200–1,500 cr from this site.** Asset turn: ~INR 500 cr+ on base paper alone.
- **Margin:** target return to **~22–25% EBITDA**; bare-minimum EBITDA next 2 yrs ~INR 125–130 cr, FY28 possibly INR 140–150 cr.
- **Debt exit:** high-cost Neo facility to be replaced/refinanced in **~15–16 months** (no prepayment premium after 15 months); 4-month moratorium, no principal for 16 months, 12% cash interest near-term (16.95% effective; gap funded by additional debt at replacement).
- **Outsourcing (asset-light):** greaseproof outsourced now >300 t/month → target 500 t/month; food-services off-take network of ~10 suppliers.
- **Pricing target:** new release/glassine paper NSR creep toward INR 130–140/kg within this FY / early next (vs base paper INR 110–120).
- **Investor meet:** in-person plant visit in Ayodhya in **October 2026** (soft-commission Jagriti by Sep quarter-end).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: - Not an order-book business; "pipeline" = capacity ramp + commercial offtake. Key visibility items: outsourced greaseproof scaling 300→500 t/month; ~10 food-services contract-mfg suppliers; US pipeline "opened significant" by US team (this year = trial run); flexible-paper offtake — ambition "5 major brands + 5 major converters buying regularly."
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Flexible / barrier-coated paper (the "holy grail"):** non-metallized flexible at pilot stage (lab pilots done, costs down, efficacy up); chemistry hard (viscosity/temperature/drying); strategy shift — make the non-porous base paper and let **converters** do barrier coating/printing (avoid cannibalizing converter relationships) rather than coating in-house. Metallized continues but goal is non-metallized (home-compostable, recyclable, marine/terrestrial-safe). Plastic flexibles sell INR 250–300/kg vs base paper INR 110–120 — large value uplift if cracked.
- **Release / glassine paper:** low-silicon-absorbance release paper + see-through glassine grade; European pilot-machine trials over next couple of months; NSR INR 130–150 (European) vs INR 110 (local).
- **US market:** "very strong demand," team opened pipeline; FY26 a trial run; near-shoring/Guatemala paused, supply from India, Pakka Inc. kept alive.
- **UP state subsidy:** ~INR 12 cr/year approved by UP cabinet (recurring benefit once plant runs).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: This was a candid turnaround/apology call: FY26 was a year of self-inflicted setbacks, a botched funding plan, a 40-day PM3 outage, pricing-war NSR erosion, and a loss-making, write-off-laden Chuk/food-services unit. Management has narrowed focus to "stabilize India first" (Guatemala and US near-shoring paused), and the entire equity case now hinges on commissioning Project Jagriti by ~Sep 2026 and cracking the high-value flexible/release-paper code, with management targeting a return to ~22
